name: lineage_get_context
description: Returns the current database context including loaded schemas, stats, and active UI filters.

name: lineage_search_objects
description: Search database objects by name or column (substring or regex). Returns object IDs, metadata, `by_type` counts, `in_user_filter`, and `name_match` (`unique` or `ambiguous` IDs, in-filter first). If an in-filter search returns no matches, widen `schemas` on subsequent calls. Use `lineage_search_ddl` to search SQL text.

query.description: In substring mode: any part of an object or column name, without a schema prefix like '[dbo].'. In regex mode: the pattern, used verbatim. May be empty ONLY together with schemas[] to list everything in those schemas.

schemas.description: Optional schema-name filter; combine with a zero-length query to list objects in those schemas.

mode.description: Name matching strategy: "substring" (default) or "regex" (case-insensitive, matched against name and schema.name).

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.

name: lineage_get_scope_bundle
description: Retrieves bounded graph scope for multi-object lineage inquiries. In `nodes[]`, the origin separates neighbors into `in` (upstream, writes into origin) and `out` (downstream, reads from origin); each node specifies `uh` and `dh` distances from the origin (0 for origin itself). `edges` lists [source, target, type] tuples. Set `include_ddl` to include object definitions. Use `lineage_get_object_detail` for single-object queries.

origin.description: Canonical object ID at the center of the requested lineage scope.

upstream_depth.description: Upstream levels: a positive integer, "all" for the whole chain, or 0 to exclude upstream. Use the smallest depth that answers the question: 1 for direct neighbours; "all" only for a whole-chain or path question.

downstream_depth.description: Downstream levels: a positive integer, "all" for the whole chain, or 0 to exclude downstream. Use the smallest depth that answers the question: 1 for direct neighbours; "all" only for a whole-chain or path question.

include_ddl.description: Whether to include SQL bodies for nodes in the returned scope.

name: lineage_start_exploration
description: Proposes a hop-by-hop exploration from `origin` for user approval, or revises its pending proposal via `proposalRevision`.

origin.description: Canonical object ID that anchors a fresh exploration.

question.description: The user question this exploration must answer.

levels.description: Starting level count for this side, or "all" for the full chain.

exactness.description: "exact" is a limit the user stated, enforced as a border. "approximate" is your own estimate, shown on the plan; above 0 it does not bound the scope, which runs until the filters or the border stop it.

levels.description: Starting level count for this side, or "all" for the full chain.

exactness.description: "exact" is a limit the user stated, enforced as a border. "approximate" is your own estimate, shown on the plan; above 0 it does not bound the scope, which runs until the filters or the border stop it.

depth.description: Starting scope: {upstream, downstream}, each {levels, exactness}. Upstream reaches sources; downstream reaches consumers. Per side: complete chain → "all", "exact"; user-stated count ("direct" = 1) → that count, "exact"; otherwise → 3, "approximate". Set 0 only when the user closes that side; it stays closed for the session. Positive approximate counts are estimates, not scope limits; filters and borders still apply. Required for a fresh proposal; omit on refine to keep reviewed depth.

excludeTypes.description: Object types excluded from the approved scope. Omit to keep the current list (on a fresh proposal, the types the GUI filter hides); a sent list replaces it.

excludeSchemas.description: Schema names excluded from the approved scope. Omit to keep the current list (on a fresh proposal, the schemas the GUI filter hides); a sent list replaces it, so repeat those you keep.

excludeNodeIds.description: Resolved object IDs to remove, including dependent branches reachable only through them. Omit to keep the current list (on a fresh proposal, the objects the GUI filter excludes); a sent list replaces it.

passNodeIds.description: Resolved object IDs to keep as topology-only passthrough nodes without analyzing them; the mapping for objects the user said to ignore or skip. Omit to keep the current list; a sent list replaces it.

scopeNotes.description: Constraints the user stated that no filter field expresses (e.g. "ignore filter criteria"), one short note each in the user's terms; echoed at the approval gate and carried to every hop.

mission_brief.description: Compact investigation goal and relevance criteria preserved verbatim across exploration hops. Keep it compact (a few sentences); length is never a rejection axis.

classification.description: Answer lens selected from primary user intent. "business": domain meaning, purpose, impact, or business rules (default when ambiguous or unspecified). Incidental SQL, table or schema mentions, or a small technical subquestion, do not change a primary business lens. "technical": execution mechanics, indexes, performance, query shapes, or loading patterns. "both": explicitly requested dual perspective. Required for fresh proposals.

analysisMode.description: Required for fresh exploration: "bb" traces whole objects; "ct" traces named columns. Default to "bb" when unclear.

targetColumns.description: CT only: name each column to trace. When the user asked for every column, read them with lineage_get_object_detail and send each one. BB forbids this property.

items.description: A field of a table or view that the user named verbatim; a column trace starts only when at least one such column is named. Wildcards are rejected at the boundary.

name: lineage_present_result
description: Renders the final report and diagram in the lineage panel: structured report sections (labels map to node badges), notes, and color highlights (`source`, `transform`, `target`). Follow-up updates can modify text, prune (`prune_node_ids`), or reveal nodes (`add_node_ids`).

name.description: Name for the generated lineage view.

summary.description: One-line summary shown with the generated view.

intro.description: Optional grounded introduction to the final report.

closing.description: Closing synthesis. Length is never a rejection axis.

prune_node_ids.description: ONLY permitted during Completed Phase follow-ups. Strictly forbidden during the initial Synthesis Phase.

add_node_ids.description: ONLY permitted during Completed Phase follow-ups. Strictly forbidden during the initial Synthesis Phase.

label.description: Legend label describing the shared graph role or status; presentation style: see the `highlights` output template.

color.description: Flow role or status. `source`: upstream origins feeding the flow. `target`: destination or focal object. `transform`: intermediate nodes that transform values. `good` / `warn` / `fail`: diagnostic status. One role per group.

node_ids.description: Node IDs that share this graph role or status.

highlight_groups.description: REQUIRED, at least 1 group. For zero-trace or single-node results, use color "target" on the origin/result node.

sections.description: Final report sections. Omit entirely to keep the committed report; list a label with no text to keep that section unchanged.

label.description: What the section's nodes share, as heading and badge (30 chars). No object names. Unique after trimming, whitespace collapse and lowercasing.

node_ids.description: Nodes this section documents; put each node in one section. Omit to keep the committed links for this label; an empty array unlinks them.

text.description: Detail body. Omit to keep the committed text for this label; supply it only to rewrite that section.

node_id.description: Node ID the caption sits below.

caption.description: One-sentence caption, grounded in the evidence supplied for this stage.

is_update.description: True only when updating an existing presentation.

name: lineage_get_object_detail
description: Fetches full definition, column metadata, and direct neighbors for a single object. For multi-object inquiries, use `lineage_get_scope_bundle`.

id.description: Canonical object ID returned by a lineage search or scope tool.

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.

name: lineage_detect_graph_patterns
description: Analyzes the entire graph for specific structural patterns such as hubs, islands, orphans, longest paths, cycles, or external references. Graph edges point upstream to downstream: inDegree counts incoming links from objects this node depends on; outDegree counts outgoing links to objects that depend on this node. Island results exclude singletons and components above the effective size limit; orphan results identify isolated nodes.

min_degree.description: Minimum node degree for hub detection.

max_size.description: Maximum nodes per island component (islands only); capped by the graph node limit. Omit to use the configured island-size limit.

name: lineage_search_ddl
description: Searches view, procedure, and function bodies via regex. Returns matching lines with object ID, line number, matched text, surrounding context, `commented` (when inside SQL comment), and `enclosing_predicate` (when governed by IF/WHILE). `by_object` summarizes counts. Use `lineage_search_objects` for object names.

query.description: Regular expression against SQL body text; case-insensitive; `^` and `$` match per line.

types.description: Optional body-type filter; omit to search all three.

name: lineage_get_screen_state
description: Returns what is on screen: active trace, graph analysis, applied bookmark, and view. Optional `ids` recall objects from a stored AI run; optional `filter` lists pruned, open_leads, or stale. `ids` and `filter` need a stored run; without one they answer `no_run_memory`. Omit input for the screen card.

ids.description: Canonical object ids to recall from the stored run, taken from the screen card's node_ids. Use without filter.

filter.description: One class of the stored run to list: pruned, open_leads, or stale. Use without ids.

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.
